summary: A 1934 Aermotor lookout on the De Soto National Forest, the central tower of the Chickasawhay district until 1989 and now part of the Wausau Work Center.

facts.design: 100-foot Aermotor tower with 7 by 7 foot cab

events.note: Built by Company 231 stationed at Camp F-4
Served as the central tower for the Chickasawhay Ranger District until 1989
Registered as NHLR US 432 (MS 2) on September 15, 2002

evidence.quote: The 100' Aermotor tower with 7' x 7' cab

evidence.supports: built 1934 by Company 231 stationed at Camp F-4
evidence.quote: Built in 1934 by Company 231 stationed at Camp F-4

evidence.supports: central tower for Chickasawhay Ranger District until 1989
evidence.quote: served as the central tower for the Chickasawhay Ranger District, De Soto National Forest until 1989

evidence.supports: part of historic Wausau Work Center; only remaining lookout on the district
evidence.quote: is part of the historic Wausau Work Center and the only remaining lookout on the district

evidence.supports: De Soto National Forest established June 15, 1936, after the 1934 tower
Chickasawhay Ranger District listed as cooperator

sources.title: Wausau Lookout Tower
sources.publisher: National Historic Lookout Register (American Resources, Inc. and Forest Fire Lookout Association)

notes_for_editor: Built year and design come from the NHLR register alone. The register says Aermotor tower but not steel, so the record's steel material (material_from design) is not confirmed by the register and was not used in the story. Current condition rests on the register's present-tense Work Center wording; the record's standing status is not independently checked. No access or staffing source was found. The 1936 forest date is from Wikipedia and should be checked against a Forest Service history before publishing. Company 231 is named as the register gives it; the story does not name a program. Two WebSearch queries and four reads were used.
